name: @w6w-apps/giphy
description: Search GIPHY's GIF and sticker library, fetch trending and random picks, translate a phrase into a GIF, and look up GIFs by id.

w6w.longDescription:
GIPHY is the GIF and sticker library most chat and social products embed, and its public API is a read-only, key-authenticated search surface over that library.

This app covers it end to end: search GIFs and stickers by phrase, list what is trending, pull a random pick, translate a phrase into the single best GIF GIPHY can find, look up one GIF by id or up to a hundred by id at once, and read the category tree. Every response is GIPHY's own envelope — `data`, plus `meta` (which is where GIPHY states its real status) and `pagination` on the list endpoints.

The API key travels as a required query-string parameter, `api_key` — GIPHY has no header-based auth option at all — so the connection's `sign` hook merges it into each request's existing query string rather than stamping a header. That is why the key is signed in one place and never enters an action.

One response-code quirk is worth knowing before you use it: GIPHY echoes its own status into the body's `meta.status`, so a call can answer HTTP 200 while the body says 401. Every success/failure decision in this app reads the body, never the status line. A health check reads GIPHY's real Statuspage feed, so a vendor incident and an expired key are reported as the different problems they are.
